newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Brussels bourse to extend bull run.
newsitem.headline: Brussels bourse to extend bull run.

text.p: The Brussels bourse took off in bullish trading on Friday, propelled forward by rises in neigbouring bourses, the Dow and a stronger dollar.
The outlook for the bourse was positive with dealers expecting the index to continue surging ahead before Christimas.
The Bel-20 share index closed up 0.49 percent or 9.21 points at 1,887.24, a new closing high. It set a new intraday high of 1,892.67 during the day.
Financials recovered from recent days of profit taking. Cyclicals also swung back into favour, dealers said, but some suffered late in the day from investors taking profits.
Steel maker Cockerill Sambre climbed 2.38 percent to 129 francs, regaining some strength after weeks of losses.

"People are shopping around for cheap stock now that so many shares have risen to record levels and Cockerill is a clear example of this, despite rumours that it will leave the Bel-20 in December," said a steel analyst.
He also said that interest was picking up in the steel sector since the economic growth picture for 1997 was improving.
Shares in steel wire and cord maker Bekaert fell 0.96 percent to 25,900 francs. One dealer said its price was too high and this might explain the drop.
Non-ferrous metals producer Union Miniere was up 1.17 percent at 2,155 francs, helped by the increased interest in cyclicals, dealers said.
Bank holding DEXIA CC climbed 2.86 percent to 2,880 francs. Dealers said it was an exciting stock with a lot of liquidity.
One trader said French truck strikes had not yet had a direct effect on the market but expected Belgian firms linked to France to suffer some lingering effects in coming weeks.
Dealers said index could touch the 2,000 level in a couple of months.
